To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Feynman rule for a gauge particle in the Feynham gauge is altered by the presence of dielectric medium, while the rules for all other couplings are left unchanged; (b) this result is obtained for any cavity, including the sphere; (c) the Feynham rule for a gauge boson in the Feynhan gauge, in a spherical cavity, is obtained in terms of the Bessel functions of the first kind, Jn (x);
(1) The Feynman rules in a cavity are derived from the path integral.
the Feynman diagram rules for gauge fields, in the presence of an arbitrary dielectric medium, are the same as the Feynman diagrams in vacuum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1. The development of the Feynman Rules for gauge fields in dielectric media,
developing a formalism for the path integral of a quantum field theory in the presence of an arbitrary dielectric medium.
the study of the effects of a dielectric on the gauge field propagator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in any gauge the Feynman rule for the gauge field couplings to the matter fields are left unalched by the presence of the dielectric medium.
in any gauge only the propagator of the gauge particle is modified, while all the other Feynman rules are left unaldered.
the Feynman diagrams are unaltered in the presence of dielectric material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Feynman diagrams for the gauge field couplings, in the presence of dielectric media, are the same as those for the free space case, while those for the gauge particles in the presence of the dielectric medium are different from those in the free space case.

the gauge field propagators in a cavity are given by those in free space multiplied by the appropriate dielectric function, and all the gauge field couplings remain unchanged.
-
the presence of a medium does not change the Feynman diagrams for the gauge field, but it does change the gauge particle propagators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Feynman diagrams are gauge independent.
the presence of a medium is not an obstacle in developing Feynman rules, as is sometimes believed.

the Feynman diagrams for gauge fields in an arbitrary medium can be derived from the corresponding Feynman diagrams in the vacuum by simply replacing the gauge field propagator in the Feynham rules by the corresponding propagator in the medium.
